entities.summary:
Khaba was a pharaoh of Ancient Egypt, active during the 3rd Dynasty of the Old Kingdom period. The exact time during which Khaba ruled is unknown but may have been around 2670 BC, and almost definitely towards the end of the dynasty.

As a ruler, Khaba was part of a larger complex of pharaohs who shaped the course of Ancient Egyptian history. He is known for his efforts to consolidate power and establish a strong economy, which had significant impacts on the development of Ancient Egyptian society.

The legacy of Khaba can be seen in the many architectural achievements of his reign, including the construction of temples and tombs that have survived to this day. His reign also saw the rise of a powerful priestly class, which played a significant role in shaping Ancient Egyptian culture.

Despite the significance of Khaba's reign, much of what is known about him comes from fragmented and often unreliable sources. This has led to ongoing debates among historians about the accuracy of our understanding of his life and reign.
